messages:
oliver: heads up — I ran the cache-hit-aware packing experiment on canary yesterday and we saw an unexpected p99 regression. attaching the short trace dump and profiler summary. :eyes:

ana: pinging infra crew. can you paste the profiler output?

oliver: sure. key bits below — this is a 2k seq workload, mixed prefixes. cache-aware packing tried to pack cache-hit requests together to increase KV reuse.

```
# profiler summary (canary, 1765000000)
p50: 45ms p95: 120ms p99: 320ms (baseline had p99 180ms)
throughput tokens/sec: 1.8M -> 1.6M (drop)
kernel time breakdown:
  matmul_fast: 68%
  attention_kv: 9%  # more due to cache merge logic
  ffn: 18%
  other: 5%
queueing: avg wait 12ms -> 18ms
batch sizes: mean 14 -> 18 (cache-aware)
cache hit ratio: 0.42 -> 0.68 (for packed groups)
```

sam: interesting. so cache hits went up but p99 did too. do we have per-batch token budget distribution? might be that cache-hit batches are larger and push out mixed batches with short targets.

jess: +1. last time we saw something similar it was due to token-budget imbalance: large batches with many cached prefixes still had long generation tails and blocked the fast small requests.

oliver: here's a snippet of our queue policy (simplified):

```
# current policy
- group by prefix-hash
- allow max_batch_tokens = 2048
- form batch when either: count>=16 or tokens >= max_batch_tokens or wait >= 20ms
- cache-aware: prefer to add same-prefix requests first
```

maria: do we track per-request expected gen length? if not, cache-aware packing will happily join 8 long-gen cached-prefix requests and starve 20 short noncached ones.

oliver: we don't use expected length in packing right now. we only estimated prefix KV hit probability. experiment was naive: prefer same-prefix until batch token limit.

sam: proposal: add token-budget targets per batch that consider both prefix_hit_fraction and expected_generation_tokens. heuristics: cap batch token budget for cache-heavy groups to smaller value so they don't monopolize GPU.

ana: can you sketch the math? I want to understand tradeoffs.

sam: quick sketch:

- per-request expected tokens = historical median tail tokens for the route (T_i)
- for a candidate group G, expected batch tokens = sum(T_i*(1 - hit_i)) + prefix_tokens (prefix KV already cached so cheap)
- enforce batch_expected_tokens <= B_target (dynamic)
- B_target = alpha * baseline_target where alpha decreases as cache_hit_fraction increases

So alpha = 1 - beta * cache_hit_fraction, beta in [0.2, 0.6]. Example: cache_hit=0.6, beta=0.5 -> alpha=0.7 -> smaller target.

jess: that looks reasonable. also add a minimum fairness window: if a noncached request waits > X ms, escalate it into the next batch regardless of packing.

oliver: logged a small POC that implements expected tokens and fairness-window. initial run (A/B) results: p99 for small routes recovered from 320ms -> 190ms, overall throughput marginally up. full profiler below: 

```
# POC A/B (24h)
p99 small-route: 320ms -> 190ms
overall p50/p95 stable
tokens/sec: 1.6M -> 1.62M
GPU utilization: unchanged
queue wait stdev: reduced
```

infra-bot: deploy-status: canary POC -> success; rolled to 10% traffic. :white_check_mark:

maria: nice. did you notice any kernel selection churn? cache-aware packing changes sequence length distribution per batch which can flip heuristics for matmul kernels.

oliver: good call — we saw a small spike in kernel selection decision time, some extra kernel jit path triggers. profiler line: kernel-selection overhead +2ms avg per batch.

sam: could be because we changed batch size distribution; for certain sequence-length ranges we pick a different matmul tile. solution: rehearse kernel selection offline with synthetic distributions from the packing policy to prewarm caches. or memoize selection for (seq_len, batch_size) pairs for a short TTL.

jess: memoizing seems low-risk. add a fallback metric to invalidate if execution latency deviates >10% from memo prediction.

ana: what's the rollout plan? we should not flip default packing until we have fairness window + token budget cap + memoized kernel mapping.

oliver: agreed. I'll open a PR with feature flags: cache_packing_v2, token_budget_cap, fairness_window_ms, kernel_memo_ttl. will include telemetry for per-route p99, tail queue wait, kernel-selection misses. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123 (WIP)

sam: add an eval that replays a 24h production trace with synthetic prefixes to get a stable estimate of p99 and throughput before canary. also add unit tests for the math.

maria: bonus: maybe we can expose a per-route config in Console to tune beta for high-latency-sensitive routes.

oliver: thanks all. action items:
- oliver: PR + canary flags today
- sam: trace replay harness + tests (ETA 2 days)
- jess: fairness-window + metrics dashboard widgets (ETA 1 day)
- ana/infra: kernel memoization sketch (ETA 3 days)

ana: also file a postmortem if we see any regression after rollout. keep an eye on region-specific patterns — APAC had slightly different prefix distributions last week.

oliver: will do. TL;DR: cache-hit-aware packing helps aggregate KV reuse but without token-budget control and fairness it can increase p99 for short requests. next iterate adds expected token budgeting + fairness + kernel memo. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
